isTheEqualityRELATIONright.theRelation: Two emissions are the same finding exactly when their admitted FindingIdentityInputV1 values are byte-identical after opensip-canonical-json-v1: same stable ruleId, same ruleMajor, same stabilityClass, same typed subject (schemaId plus canonical value), same typed canonical proof anchor (schemaId plus canonical value).
isTheEqualityRELATIONright.myAdjudication: DEFENSIBLE, and it is the relation I would have chosen. Every one of the three failure modes the brief names is answered in the direction that protects ratchet, and the one that cannot be answered by a hash is answered by a REJECTION rather than by a guess.
isTheEqualityRELATIONright.lineNumbersExcluded: CORRECT and the strongest single choice in the design. Absolute line, column, startByte and endByte are excluded in EVERY stability class including span-fallback, which is stricter than most implementations would dare. I verified by construction: no vector's identityInput contains any offset, and FV-06/FV-07 move line 20 to 200 and bytes 400/4000 with a byte-identical digest.
isTheEqualityRELATIONright.filePathsHandled: CORRECT, and better than a binary include/exclude. Path is excluded outright for rename-stable, and admitted for path-stable and span-fallback ONLY inside a typed subject or anchor schema -- never as a universal top-level field. The classes are honest about what they promise: path-stable says renames re-report, and says so in its own cost line rather than claiming rename stability it cannot deliver. FV-04/FV-05 pin the rename moving the digest, which is the honest behaviour, not a defect.
isTheEqualityRELATIONright.tooLittleIncluded: THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION IS IDENTIFIED BY NAME AND ANSWERED BY REJECTION, NOT BY A HASH. excludedFieldTrades row 5 states it verbatim: 'That is the dangerous direction: one can be silently suppressed by a baseline.' The design's answer is that inability to construct distinct canonical anchors is FINDING_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS and the partition is REJECTED -- never deduplicated, never salted, never collapsed. Choosing a visible failure over a silent suppression is the correct trade and it is the trade I would defend.
isTheEqualityRELATIONright.butSeeAdvisoryA4: The rejection is enforceable within one rule partition and is NOT enforceable across runs against a stored baseline. See advisories.A-4.

findingIdDerivedVersusAllocated.didItCONFLATEtheTwoQuestions: NO. This was the sharpest thing I was asked to check and the artifact handles it correctly. findingIdDecision is a separate block from valueDigestRecipe, it states four things derivation buys and three it costs, three things allocation would buy, and it rejects allocation on LIFECYCLE REQUIREMENTS rather than by analogy.
findingIdDerivedVersusAllocated.theProjectIdComparison: Handled correctly and explicitly, and it is the opposite of a conflation. Verbatim: 'ProjectId is correctly allocated because its owning host surface defines and persists that lifecycle. A FindingValue in this pure return value has the opposite requirements.' It does not reason 'ProjectId is allocated, therefore identities are allocated'; it compares what each lifecycle needs and finds them opposite. threat-model.v3's storageNamespace treatment of ProjectId as a solved allocated instance is therefore not misappropriated.
findingIdDerivedVersusAllocated.myAdjudication: CORRECT, and I believe forced rather than chosen given the unchanged v1.6 API -- though the artifact more modestly grades it author-choice. Three independent reasons: CoreDeps forbids entropy and storage, so a CSPRNG allocation is simply unreachable from the closed evaluate inputs; policyOutcome.derivationDigest COMMITS findingId through the FindingValueV1 record at tag 0xc2, which I verified by re-encoding, so a fresh allocation would make two identical evaluations produce different derivationDigests and destroy the deterministic-retry property R-1 exists to guarantee; and a persistent allocation would introduce a store authority into the pure core, which freeze 6 law 5 and law 8 both forbid.
findingIdDerivedVersusAllocated.theCostItAcceptsAndDeclares: findingId carries zero information beyond valueDigest. R-1's FindingValue is now a three-field record with two independent degrees of freedom, and FindingList.orderRule's tuple (ruleId, findingId, valueDigest) has two functionally dependent components. The artifact anticipates this objection verbatim at strongestObjectionsExpected[2] and answers it as intentional type/address redundancy forced by the unchanged three-field shape. I accept the answer.
findingIdDerivedVersusAllocated.scopeOfForceIsStatedHonestly: 'Derived is forced only while preserving the v1.6 R-1 API and deterministic evidence promise... this candidate does not claim allocation is universally wrong.' That is the correct scoping and it is rarer than it should be.

canonicalisationInheritance.doesItLEANONCJ_R12: NO, and this is the single sharpest thing it gets right about its inheritance. The strings CJ-R12 and CJ-R appear ZERO times in the candidate. It never cites the rule, never quotes its VECTOR-FORCED grade, and never claims float rejection is vector-backed at the encoder. What it does instead is enforce float rejection at ADMISSION -- hostComputationOrder step 4 rejects floats before canonicalisation, admissionBeforeEncoding rejects wrong exact scalar types 'before a byte is hashed', and floatRule states 'No float is ever rounded, stringified or coerced to an integer. It rejects.' That is precisely where the canonical-JSON review's advisory A-1 says the rule genuinely IS forced. The candidate inherits the strong half and not the weak half, apparently without knowing the advisory existed.
canonicalisationInheritance.undeterminedRegisterHandling: It cites UR-1 through UR-5 BY NAME and constrains its own inputs so each undetermined corner is unreachable rather than silently resolved: UR-1 by requiring ASCII member names in production rule-family schemas until the ordering plane is settled; UR-2 by bounding ruleMajor to positive U64 and admitting that nested schemas needing zero, negative or wider integers have no vector evidence here; UR-3 by rejecting non-NFC at admission so normalise-versus-reject produces identical bytes for every admitted input; UR-4 by keeping every vector string ASCII and refusing to claim byte qualification for the escaping corner; UR-5 by rejecting lone surrogates before encoding.
canonicalisationInheritance.isTheUR3ARGUMENTSOUND: YES. Constraining the input domain so that both surviving readings of CJ-R10 agree on every admitted value is a legitimate way to depend on an undetermined rule without choosing it. There is a mild wording tension -- it says 'this candidate does not choose between the profile's two surviving readings' while its own admission rule IS the reject reading -- but the substance is right: it chooses for its OWN admission, which makes the encoder's undetermined behaviour unreachable, and it does not purport to settle the profile.
canonicalisationInheritance.openDepFI07: Explicitly declares profile closure for non-ASCII key ordering and control/non-ASCII escaping as an open dependency and states it 'cannot upgrade prose-stated rules into vector-forced facts.' That is the correct posture toward an inheritance the dispatch warned is weaker than it looks.

section51AndTheParkProperty.requirement: invention is forbidden; any preimage field with no producing rule must be declared an OPEN DEPENDENCY, not chosen
section51AndTheParkProperty.verdict: SATISFIED, and this is the artifact's best single property. Every field it could not produce is named, with what is missing, why it was not chosen, and what an implementer may do meanwhile.
checkedFieldByField: ruleId -- OPEN-DEP-FI-01, the join to a rename-stable ContributionId. Refuses to treat a slug, package coordinate or rule-emitted text as the stable ID. Correct: that would have invented the most important preimage field.
ruleMajor -- OPEN-DEP-FI-02. Refuses to parse a contributionVersion or substitute artifactDigest, and states the two have opposite baseline behaviour. Correct.

subject schemas -- OPEN-DEP-FI-03. Refuses to choose between fact-plane namespaced subjects and evaluation-proof path-like subjects, correctly identifying that as another surface's unresolved vocabulary. Correct under law 19.

anchor schemas -- OPEN-DEP-FI-04. States why fact anchor records cannot be hashed verbatim (they carry SnapshotId, path and absolute byte bounds) and declines to manufacture rule-family keys. Correct.
stability registry -- OPEN-DEP-FI-05. 'A label without rename/line-shift controls would be an assertion, not stability evidence.' Correct and self-aware.

durable Finding/baseline schema -- OPEN-DEP-FI-06. Declines to add fields outside R-1's three-field completion value or to design baseline custody, on the ground that it would exceed R-1 authority. Correct under law 19.
section51AndTheParkProperty.didItSILENTLYPICKANYPARKEDVALUE: NO. I checked every preimage field against the two measurement sweeps' classifications and against freeze 7.1's park property. The test: schemaIds in the vectors are all prefixed test: and the artifact declares 'Every schemaId beginning test: and every test:* identity below is fixture-only... Unknown production schemaId rejects.' The fixtures do not smuggle a production mapping, which was the specific thing I was asked to look for.
section51AndTheParkProperty.doesItCLAIMTOCLOSETHEPARKROW: NO, and it is careful about the distinction. implementationBoundary separates what crates/core can compute now (the generic function, both output fields, all seven vectors, the repaired literals) from what cannot be claimed (production integration, durable baseline), and calls the gain 'narrower than full blocker closure' in strongestObjectionsExpected[4]. The honest reading is that IL4-12's first-commit blocker is DISCHARGED AS TO THE ALGORITHM and NOT as to production integration, which is exactly what the artifact says.

law18.atTheIDENTITYboundary: HELD. ruleMajor is typed 'exact JSON integer' with 'boolean and floating point reject before numeric comparison'; the closed enum stabilityClass rejects non-members; the encoder rejects floats and non-string keys. I verified each by construction: 1 vs "1" vs true all separate, and 1.0 rejects.
law18.inTHESEbytes: The candidate's own parseDiscipline mandates bool-before-int classification and non-finite rejection through parse_constant, and I confirmed the resulting figures independently at 4 booleans and 46 integers. Its operationAccounting and measurement counts are canonical decimal STRINGS rather than JSON numbers, which is the corpus's now-standard defence and is applied consistently.

blockers.grade: BLOCKER -- a recorded measurement in the effective successor is falsified by this candidate's own repair
blockers.rule: freeze 7.2.2: a recorded measurement gets a HARD COMPARISON; an uncompared measurement is prose that looks like evidence, and going stale is a TRUE POSITIVE about these bytes. Plus 7.2.2's AUTHORSHIP rider: rows carried unchanged from the predecessor must be read against THIS file's claims, and a row identical to its predecessor is exactly what an omitted repair looks like.
blockers.what: The candidate replaces eight literal FindingValue leaves with computed values. Two of the replacements land inside the PDD vector corpus. It then recomputes every dependent DIGEST correctly -- and does not recompute the dependent MEASUREMENTS of that same corpus.
blockers.theMeasurement: The longest text component across the seventeen policy-derivation vectors.
blockers.why: The new findingId is 'finding:' (8 bytes) + 'sha256:' (7) + 64 hex = 79 bytes, at PDD-03.recordValue.findings[0].findingId. The previous maximum was a 71-byte Digest. The repair introduced the longest text component in the corpus and nothing re-measured it.
threePositionsAffected: $.policyDerivationIdentity.primitives.text.measuredHeadroom -- says 'the longest text component across all seventeen vectors is 71 bytes, THE WIDTH OF A DIGEST'. False on the number AND on the explanation: the longest is now a findingId, not a Digest.
blockers.theClassWasNEVERSWEPT: Measured on the candidate: the strings '4096', '71 bytes', 'headroom', 'measuredHeadroom', 'maxTextComponent' and 'seventeen' occur ZERO times in the whole file. No operation targets /measuredSelfReport or /policyDerivationIdentity/primitives. This is not a judgement call the author made and lost; the question was never asked.
blockers.theSUBJECTSPARTIALDEFENCEAndWhyItIsInsuf: successorContextV17.inheritedAuthoringEvidenceRule declares that 'the predecessor's parseDiscipline, measuredSelfReport and other authoring-time observations remain historical evidence about v1.6' and are 'not silently relabelled as measurements of v1.7'. That is a real defence and it is why I did not grade the whole measuredSelfReport block. It fails on two counts. First, measuredSelfReport mixes two kinds: authoring-process facts (predecessor digests, drift disclosure, shasum cross-check) which the disclaimer genuinely covers, and CONTENT measurements OF THE CONTRACT'S OWN VECTORS -- maxTextComponentBytesAcrossAllVectors is the latter, and its referent is the vector corpus the delta just edited. Second and decisively, the disclaimer names parseDiscipline, measuredSelfReport and 'authoring-time observations'. It does NOT reach policyDerivationIdentity.primitives.text.measuredHeadroom, which sits inside the NORMATIVE primitives block, in the middle of the recipe's own text rule, adjacent to the 4096 bound it is explaining. No disclaimer covers it and no operation touches it.
blockers.severityJustification: No digest moves -- 79 is far below the 4096 bound, no rejection control changes behaviour, and all 17 recomputed vectors are correct. The defect is entirely in recorded measurement, not arithmetic. It is nonetheless a blocker for APPLICATION because freeze 7.2.2 makes an uncompared, falsified recorded measurement a true positive about these bytes, because it is the precise shape of the AUTHORSHIP rider I was dispatched to test, and because it is the MIRROR IMAGE of the retention-tiers.v26 defect the freeze already records -- there the value was corrected and the prose left stale; here neither was.
blockers.repair: Three additional set operations in a v1.8: maxTextComponentBytesAcrossAllVectors '71' -> '79'; the4096BoundHeadroom 'about 57x' -> about 51.8x; and primitives.text.measuredHeadroom restated so the number is 79 and the phrase 'the width of a Digest' becomes the width of a derived findingId. Cannot be made in place under freeze 7.2. Recommend the successor also re-derive the class rather than patching these three rows, since the same question -- what else was measuring the leaves I just changed? -- is the one that was never asked.
blockers.whatWOULDHAVECAUGHTIT: Sweeping the predecessor for every recorded measurement whose REFERENT is a leaf the delta modifies, rather than for every leaf the delta modifies. The candidate did the second and not the first.

advisories.grade: ADVISORY -- a forced-versus-chosen label is wrong, in the over-claiming-originality direction
advisories.what: standingOfClaims.authorChoicesNotDerived[0] lists 'The new recipe name FINDING-VALUE-DIGEST-V1 and domain label opensip.finding-value.v1' as an author choice. The domain label genuinely is new -- 0 corpus occurrences. The RECIPE NAME is not: the exact string FINDING-VALUE-DIGEST-V1 already exists in artifacts/implementer-litmus.v4.json, which is RECORDED INPUT NUMBER 11 OF THIS CANDIDATE with a digest the candidate itself pins and I verified. It appears at IL4-12.whatIWouldNeedToProceed: 'A FINDING-VALUE-DIGEST-V1 recipe in R-1's own binding bytes, under law 19.' That is its sole corpus occurrence outside the subject.
advisories.whyItMatters: The block exists precisely to separate what the corpus forced from what the author chose. One row is mislabelled, and the artifact's own predecessor set the disclosure precedent it did not follow: v1.6's namespaceAndDomainSeparator.adoptedFrom devotes a paragraph to explaining that policy-derivation-v1 was ADOPTED from plan-and-policy-identity-recipes.v2's proposal, and why adoption by the entitled surface is lawful. The same sentence would have covered this.
advisories.whyItIsNotABlocker: The substance is untouched. The litmus named a desired recipe and defined no preimage, no domain label, no field set and no vector, so firstDesignDisclosure's claim that nothing 'previously defined HOW valueDigest or findingId is produced' is TRUE. Law 19 is unaffected -- a litmus is a report, not a binding artifact, and R-1's successor is entitled to mint the name regardless of who first wrote it down. The error over-credits the author's originality rather than under-crediting the corpus, which is the harmless direction and the opposite of the defect this corpus usually catches.
advisories.repair: One clause: note that the name was proposed in implementer-litmus.v4 IL4-12 and is adopted here by the surface entitled to write it down.

advisories.grade: ADVISORY -- two domain-separation constructions now live in one artifact, unremarked
advisories.what: The effective v1.7 carries two identity recipes with structurally different preimages. FINDING-VALUE-DIGEST-V1 uses the house form UTF8(label) || 0x00 || canonical bytes. Its sibling POLICY-DERIVATION-DIGEST-V1, carried unchanged in the same document, uses 0x30 || C(0x31, UTF8(namespace)) || C(0x32, ASCII(domain)) || C(0x33, root32) -- an EP8 componentFrame TLV construction with NO NUL separator, verified by decoding v1.6's own pinned outerPreimageHex. The candidate never notices the divergence and never justifies it.
advisories.myAdjudication: The CHOICE is right. A canonical-JSON payload belongs in the house JSON form, and PDD's TLV framing exists because it had to interoperate with evaluation-proof's grammar. Both are properly domain-separated and neither can reach the other's preimage. But a reader of the effective contract now meets two constructions in one artifact with nothing telling them why, and the corpus's own standard is that a silent choice is the one two engineers make differently.
advisories.repair: One sentence in valueDigestRecipe noting that the sibling identity in this same artifact uses EP8 componentFrame framing because its payload is a TLV record, while this identity uses the house NUL form because its payload is canonical JSON.

advisories.grade: ADVISORY -- one cell of the stability matrix is asserted, not exercised
advisories.what: The design makes three stability classes x two perturbations (rename, unrelated insertion above) into a six-cell matrix. Five cells are pinned by vectors: rename-stable under rename+insertion+message edit (FV-01/02), rename-stable under a distinct anchor (FV-03), path-stable under rename (FV-04/05), span-fallback under line and byte shift (FV-06/07). The sixth -- path-stable under an unrelated insertion -- has no vector.
advisories.measured: It holds. I constructed the pair and the digests are equal, because absolute offsets are absent from every schema in every class, so the property is true by construction.
advisories.whyItStillMatters: The corpus's own repeated finding is that a property with no vector is an assertion, and the value of these vectors is that they name the misreading they defeat. The missing cell is the one an implementer is most likely to get wrong, because path-stable is the class where a reader might assume 'path-based means position-based'.
advisories.repair: One vector, FV-08, path-stable base with a shifted excludedPresentation and a MUST-COLLIDE assertion. It costs nothing -- the digest already exists as FV-04's.

advisories.grade: ADVISORY -- the dangerous direction is guarded, but only by artifacts that do not exist yet, and the guard has a reach the artifact does not bound
advisories.what: I reproduced the collision the design most needs to prevent: two genuinely distinct violations on one subject, projected through a rule-family anchor schema carrying only a contextKey, produce one digest. The design's answer is FINDING_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS at hostComputationOrder step 7, enforced 'over all emitted findings' before the rule partition is accepted.
advisories.theBoundTHEARTIFACTDOESNOTSTATE: That check is a WITHIN-PARTITION check. It fires when both colliding emissions are present in the same evaluation. It cannot fire in the case baseline/ratchet actually exposes: a digest stored in a baseline from run 1 suppressing a genuinely different finding in run 2, when the colliding sibling is not co-emitted in run 2. In that case there is no second emission to compare against and nothing detects the suppression. The artifact's excludedFieldTrades correctly names 'runtime ambiguity rejection' as one of three guards, but only one of the three -- closed per-rule-family anchor schemas (OPEN-DEP-FI-04) and distinctness qualification (OPEN-DEP-FI-05) -- is the one that would cover the cross-run case, and both are open dependencies.
advisories.isThisADEFECT: Not in the design, which cannot solve it without the anchor schemas, and not in the disclosure, since implementationBoundary.cannotBeClaimedYet names OPEN-DEP-FI-01 through -05 as unresolved and refuses to claim production readiness. It is recorded because a signer reading includedFieldTrades and ambiguityAndCollisionRules could reasonably come away believing the dangerous direction is CLOSED, and it is not -- it is DEFERRED, correctly, to two artifacts that do not exist.
advisories.repair: State the within-partition scope of the step 7 check explicitly, and say that cross-run baseline suppression is guarded by OPEN-DEP-FI-04/-05 and by nothing else.

advisories.grade: ADVISORY -- an inherited grammar under-determination that this candidate depends on and does not name
advisories.what: The candidate's 21 arithmetic operations re-encode PDD-03 and PDD-13 under v1.6's recordGrammar. That grammar declares recordTag values 0x80/0xa0/0xb0/0xc0/0xd0 and encodes nested records as 'C(0x8b, RuleValueV1 complete record bytes)' -- but never states in words that the record tag byte is INSIDE 'complete record bytes'. Written from the prose alone, my first encoder omitted the tags and failed 17 of 17 v1.6 vectors. The point is recoverable only from the two published completeRecordHex strings on PDD-01 and PDD-17.
advisories.whoOwnsIt: v1.6, not this candidate. It is inherited and unedited, and this review is not a review of v1.6.
advisories.whyItIsRECORDEDHERE: Because the candidate's central claim about its own arithmetic -- that the two repaired vectors are 're-encoded under inherited v1.6 grammar' -- rests on a grammar clause that a second implementer reading the prose gets wrong on the first attempt. It happens to be recoverable, which is why this is an advisory rather than a finding, and it is exactly the shape freeze 7.1 consequence 3 names: a binding head whose digests no contract reader can recompute from the words alone. A successor could close it in one clause.
advisories.repair: In a future R-1 successor: state that the record tag byte is the first byte of a record's complete bytes and is included in the enclosing component frame's length.
